messages:
maya: Hey support — our rerank calls started returning unexpected order today. Using TS SDK v0.9.2. Some items with higher relevance are at the bottom and score values look like "0.0" or occasionally >1. Request id: req_3a7f9. Any idea?

sam: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a minimal repro (payload + SDK call) and the raw API response body if you have it? Also what model / rerank params are you using?

maya: repro below. model: rwrk-large-001, temperature: 0.0, top_k: 10. We call client.rerank({query, candidates}) using the ts-sdk. SDK call:```ts
await client.rerank({
  query: "how to reset password",
  candidates: candidatesList // array of {id, text}
});
```

Raw response snippet (from sdk): ```json
{"results":[{"id":"c3","score":"0.2"},{"id":"c1","score":"0.8"},{"id":"c2","score":"1.2"}]}
```

Note: c1 should be top, but appears in middle. Also score for c2 > 1 which seems wrong compared to previous runs.

eli: thanks — two quick checks: 1) can you call the HTTP API directly (curl) to see if ordering differs from SDK? 2) confirm whether your candidatesList order is preserved when you build the request (console.log before call).

maya: did a curl to the same endpoint with the exact JSON body and got:```json
{"results":[{"id":"c1","score":0.8},{"id":"c2","score":1.2},{"id":"c3","score":0.2}]}
```

So raw API returns correct order. That points at SDK behavior. I logged payload sent by ts-sdk (pre-serialization) and it matches my array order.

sam: ok that narrows it. eli any known regressions in 0.9.2? nina any Python parity issues?

eli: looking at recent changelog — v0.9.2 introduced a candidate normalization step for legacy compat. There's an open issue where the TypeScript client converts numeric scores to strings when serializing, and in one codepath it uses Object.entries on a candidates map which can reorder items if someone passed a plain object instead of array. If maya passed an array it should be fine, but some build tools can transform arrays -> sparse objects.

maya: I definitely passed an array. How would map/object conversion flip order?

eli: if code does `Object.fromEntries(array.map( ... ))` then later iterates over `Object.keys()` you get insertion order in modern JS but if there was any use of a plain object built from .reduce without preserving indexes it can be unstable across transforms. But given curl works, I'm suspicious of post-response parsing in the SDK too — maybe scores are parsed as strings and then compared lexicographically during client-side sorting.

nina: FYI python sdk had a prior bug where scores serialized as strings caused the client to sort using string compare, giving 10 > 2 style issues. We fixed that by coercing to float before sorting. Could be a similar regression in TS.

eli: can you run a quick experiment maya: upgrade to ts-sdk 0.9.3-alpha (install link: https://npm.redwood.dev/ts-sdk/0.9.3-alpha) or as a quicker workaround, after the call, inspect the returned results and sort by Number(score) to validate? Example:```ts
const res = await client.rerank(...)
res.results.sort((a,b) => Number(b.score) - Number(a.score))
```

maya: tried the local sort; that restores the expected order. But we need a fix on the SDK side. I can patch on our side but this is customer-facing.

eli: confirmed — reproducer + request id forwarded to infra. Found root cause: in v0.9.2 we introduced a response normalization that accidentally coerces numeric scores to strings and then calls .sort() without numeric comparator in one helper. That yields lexicographic ordering for scores. Also there was a separate path that left scores as numbers, causing mixed types in the same results array (hence sometimes >1 as string or number mismatch in logs).

sam: ETA for a fix? Any mitigation for customers?

eli: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ts-sdk/pull/842 — fixes parsing to always Number(score) and adds tests. Patch scheduled for 0.9.3 stable release tomorrow. Workarounds: 1) pin to 0.9.1 if you can't accept alpha; 2) apply client-side sort Number(score) as above; 3) call the HTTP API directly.

maya: thanks. Also noticed request latency spiked around the same time — unrelated? logs show a 503 earlier in the window.

deploy-bot: Incident INC-2026: brief control-plane degradation at 2026-03-11T14:02Z caused increased latency and one 503 for req_3a7f9. Root cause: autoscaler race. Impact limited to 2 minutes; mitigations deployed.

nina: good to know — sounds like two independent issues (latency incident + SDK parsing bug).

maya: great, we'll apply the local sort for now and plan to upgrade to 0.9.3 when out. Thanks for the quick triage! :thumbsup:

sam: closing loop — I'll follow up once 0.9.3 is published and tag you. If you want I can create a postmortem note combining INC-2026 and this SDK regression for the customer-facing timeline.

maya: please do. appreciated.
